evidence.title: Know the PM
evidence.claim: The official PMO biography states that Narendra Modi served as Prime Minister from 2019 to 2024, so he was in office throughout 2022.
evidence.locator: biography paragraph with the service dates
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official government biography; direct office-tenure claim.
evidence.period_fit: Confirms officeholding during the target year.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributes executive office to Modi, but not any specific nuclear decision.
contrary_evidence: Promotional tone and no detail on nuclear authority or 2022 conduct.

reasons.reason: Office-tenure context only; it confirms Modi held the PM office in 2022 but is not a 2022 nuclear-risk choice.

evidence.title: History
evidence.claim: The Department of Atomic Energy says it was set up under the direct charge of the Prime Minister, which makes Modi's office directly relevant to atomic-energy governance in 2022.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official government department history page; direct institutional authority claim.
evidence.period_fit: Long-running institutional structure that still applies in 2022.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Institutional authority attaches to the PM office, not to a specific personal act by Modi.
contrary_evidence: This is structural authority, not evidence of a 2022 risk-bearing choice.

evidence.title: NCA reviews nuclear capability
evidence.publisher: Press Information Bureau / Prime Minister's Office
evidence.claim: The Nuclear Command Authority under the Prime Minister's chairmanship reviewed India's nuclear capability and said it had command and control structures in place.
evidence.locator: opening paragraph of the press release
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official government press release naming the PM as NCA chair.
evidence.period_fit: Inherited command structure that remained relevant in 2022.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Shows the PM's formal nuclear authority; the 2004 text predates Modi but defines the office he later occupied.
contrary_evidence: Old source, so it establishes inherited structure rather than 2022 conduct.

reasons.reason: Inherited command-structure evidence only; use it to define baseline authority, not as direct 2022 conduct.

evidence.title: Prime Minister felicitates crew of INS Arihant on completion of Nuclear Triad
evidence.publisher: Press Information Bureau / Prime Minister's Office
evidence.claim: The PMO said India had put in place a robust nuclear command and control structure, effective safety assurance architecture, and strict political control under the Nuclear Command Authority, while remaining committed to credible minimum deterrence and no-first-use.
evidence.locator: main body of the press release
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official PMO text on command-and-control and doctrine.
evidence.ruler_attribution: This is inherited doctrine and structure, not a 2022 Modi-specific action.
contrary_evidence: It is a favorable self-description and does not prove operational perfection.

reasons.reason: Baseline self-description only; it is useful for inherited doctrine but not for target-year action.

evidence.title: INS Arihant carries out successful launch of Submarine Launched Ballistic Missile
evidence.publisher: Press Information Bureau / Ministry of Defence
evidence.claim: India said the Arihant SLBM launch validated the SSBN programme and a robust survivable assured retaliatory capability consistent with its no-first-use posture.
evidence.locator: second and third paragraphs of the release
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official 2022 government release on a nuclear-capability event.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Government-level capability maintenance under Modi; it does not show a crisis decision or doctrinal change by him personally.
contrary_evidence: Strengthening retaliatory capability can stabilize deterrence, but it also continues modernization rather than disarmament.

evidence.title: Nuclear weapons at a glance: India and Pakistan
evidence.claim: The 2022 parliamentary briefing says India is outside the NPT and CTBT, maintains a no-first-use policy, continues to produce weapons-grade fissile material, is estimated at about 160 warheads, and is actively expanding delivery capabilities.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Parliamentary research briefing synthesizing multiple public sources.
evidence.period_fit: Directly relevant to the 2022 posture and inherited baseline.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Country-level nuclear posture under Modi's tenure, but not proof of any single personal decision.
contrary_evidence: It is a synthesis rather than a primary Indian source.
It describes capability trends, not operational misuse.

reasons.reason: Country posture synthesis only; keep it as context for inherited baseline rather than personal decision evidence.

evidence.title: Nuclear Notebook: How many nuclear weapons does India have in 2022?
evidence.claim: The 2022 Nuclear Notebook estimates India at about 160 warheads, says at least four new systems are under development, and notes additional plutonium capacity plus a growing emphasis on China.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Authoritative technical nuclear-arsenal assessment by FAS experts published in the Bulletin.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Shows the inherited and continuing posture Modi governed in 2022, but not a personal crisis choice.
contrary_evidence: Estimate-based, not an official inventory.
Modernization is not itself evidence of reckless use.

reasons.reason: Technical estimate of arsenal size and modernization; context only, not ruler-specific conduct.

evidence.title: प्रधानमंत्री रूस के राष्ट्रपति के साथ द्विपक्षीय बैठक में प्रधानमंत्री श्री नरेन्द्र मोदी का उद्घाटन भाषण
evidence.publisher: Press Information Bureau / Prime Minister's Office
evidence.claim: In the original Hindi release, Modi told Putin that this is not an era of war and that democracy, diplomacy, and dialogue are the path forward.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary local-language government text from the target year.
evidence.period_fit: Directly within the target year and directly about Modi.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct ruler speech at a major geopolitical crisis moment.
contrary_evidence: This is a diplomatic statement, not a nuclear doctrine change or command-control reform.

evidence.title: No Modi-Putin summit this year after they met in September- Indian govt source
evidence.claim: Reuters reported that India did not explicitly condemn Russia's invasion, remained a major buyer of Russian oil, and that the decision not to hold the annual Modi-Putin summit was not due to the nuclear angle.
evidence.locator: Reuters report text near the lead and second paragraphs
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters reporting carried by Euronews, with an explicit government-source attribution inside the report.
evidence.period_fit: Covers late-2022 statecraft around the Ukraine war.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Reports on Modi's broader diplomatic balancing, with one factual sentence directly attributed to an Indian government source.
contrary_evidence: India stayed strategically close to Russia on trade and energy even while urging restraint.

evidence.title: Visit of the Prime Minister of the United Kingdom to India (April 21-22, 2022)
evidence.claim: Modi said the Ukraine-Russia conflict required an immediate cessation of violence and a return to direct dialogue and diplomacy as the only way forward.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official bilateral statement on the PMO site, dated in the target year.
evidence.period_fit: Direct 2022 statement during the target year.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct ruler-level diplomatic position.
contrary_evidence: Again, this is rhetorical restraint rather than a demonstrable nuclear-risk reduction measure.

evidence.title: Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi speaks on telephone with His Excellency Mr Vladimir Putin, President of the Russian Federation
evidence.publisher: Press Information Bureau / Prime Minister's Office
evidence.claim: The PMO said Modi reiterated that dialogue and diplomacy were the only way forward in the Ukraine conflict.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official PMO readout of the call, dated in the target year.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct ruler-level crisis messaging to a nuclear-armed counterpart.
contrary_evidence: It is a peace-oriented call, not proof of changes to command control or treaty posture.

evidence.title: First Committee Sends 20 Nuclear Weapons Drafts to General Assembly Requiring 33 Separate Votes for Adoption
evidence.claim: The UN First Committee record shows India abstained on the 2022 CTBT-related nuclear-disarmament text and on the broader nuclear-disarmament draft that called for a legally binding no-first-use instrument.
evidence.locator: paragraphs describing the CTBT vote and the overall nuclear-disarmament draft
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous UN voting record with explicit country vote details.
evidence.ruler_attribution: This is the government's multilateral position under Modi, but not a personal statement by him.
contrary_evidence: India continued to advocate disarmament language even while withholding support from specific texts.

evidence.title: Statement by Ambassador DB Venkatesh Varma Permanent Representative of India to the CD during the Thematic Debate on Nuclear Weapons at First Committee
evidence.publisher: Permanent Mission of India to the Conference on Disarmament in Geneva
evidence.claim: India said it remained unwaveringly committed to universal, non-discriminatory, verifiable nuclear disarmament, supported a step-by-step multilateral framework, and backed measures to reduce nuclear danger, including de-alerting and de-targeting.
evidence.locator: opening and middle paragraphs of the statement
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official Indian UN statement reproduced on the mission site; directly dated to the target year.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Government position under Modi; the statement is not personally by him but is attributable to his administration.
contrary_evidence: It is longstanding doctrine language and does not by itself prove new 2022 risk reduction on the ground.

evidence.title: Statement by Mr. Maitrey Kulkarni, Deputy Secretary (D&ISA), Ministry of External Affairs, New Delhi at the CD Plenary on Aug 11, 2022 on 'The Centrality of International Cooperation and Capacity Building in Building Safe and Secure Cyberspace'
evidence.publisher: Permanent Mission of India to the Conference on Disarmament in Geneva
evidence.claim: India said international transfers of dual-use goods and high-technology with military applications should be effectively regulated, and that it remained committed to an open, secure, stable, accessible, and peaceful cyberspace.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official 2022 Indian statement on an emerging-catastrophic-risk domain, reproduced by the mission site.
evidence.period_fit: Direct 2022 evidence for dual-use and cyber governance.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Government position under Modi; the speaker is an MEA official rather than Modi personally.
contrary_evidence: This is policy language, not proof of effective implementation or transparency in practice.

evidence.title: Joint Statement
evidence.publisher: Press Information Bureau / Ministry of Defence
evidence.claim: India and China said their troops in the Gogra-Hotsprings area had begun disengaging in a coordinated and planned way, conducive to peace and tranquility in the border areas.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary 2022 government statement on an actual de-escalation event.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributed to the Modi government’s border policy and military diplomacy, not to a specific personal order.
contrary_evidence: Residual border tensions with China remained unresolved after the disengagement.

evidence.title: Security Council Calls Emergency Special Session of General Assembly on Ukraine Crisis, Adopting Resolution 2623 (2022) by 11 Votes in Favour, 1 Against, 3 Abstentions
evidence.claim: The Security Council called an emergency special session on Ukraine and India abstained on Resolution 2623 (2022).
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous UN vote record naming India.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Shows the government’s multilateral stance under Modi, but not a personal speech or order.
contrary_evidence: Abstention does not equal support for aggression, but it also stopped short of explicit condemnation.

evidence.title: Security Council Fails to Adopt Draft Resolution on Ending Ukraine Crisis, as Russian Federation Wields Veto
evidence.claim: India said it was disturbed by developments in Ukraine, called for an immediate cessation of hostilities, emphasized the UN Charter and territorial integrity, and said dialogue was the only way to settle disputes before abstaining.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous UN meeting record with India's explicit explanation of vote.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Government position under Modi through India’s UN mission, not a direct personal statement.
contrary_evidence: India did not join the condemnation bloc or sanctions regime.

evidence.title: Security Council Fails to Adopt Resolution Condemning Moscow's Referenda in Ukraine’s Occupied Territories, as Permanent Member Employs Veto
evidence.claim: India abstained on the draft resolution condemning the referenda and purported annexation of occupied Ukrainian territories.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous UN vote record naming India.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Reflects the government’s cautious multilateral stance under Modi.
contrary_evidence: The abstention preserved ties with Russia while limiting explicit alignment with the condemning bloc.

evidence.title: English Translation of Remarks by Prime Minister, Shri Narendra Modi at the SCO Summit
evidence.publisher: Press Information Bureau / Prime Minister's Office
evidence.claim: Modi said the Ukraine crisis had created an energy and food crisis and urged stronger SCO cooperation, mutual trust, and full transit rights among members.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary 2022 PMO translation of the Prime Minister’s remarks.
evidence.period_fit: Directly within the target year and directly attributable to Modi.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct ruler speech; it reflects Modi’s public diplomatic position.
contrary_evidence: The remarks are broad regional diplomacy, not proof of concrete conflict settlement.
They do not resolve the Russia-Ukraine war or border disputes by themselves.

evidence.title: Blinken urges Indian FM not to buy additional Russian oil
evidence.claim: Reuters reported that the United States urged India not to increase Russian oil purchases, while noting India had already bought at least 13 million barrels of Russian crude since the invasion and had not imposed sanctions on Russia.
evidence.locator: story text summary in the Reuters archive record
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters reporting with a contemporaneous archival record and explicit sourcing from U.S. and Indian officials.
evidence.period_fit: Directly within the target year, shortly after the invasion.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Not a personal order from Modi, but a strong indicator of the government’s balancing between peace rhetoric and material ties to Russia.
contrary_evidence: Energy security can explain some of the trade, but it still weakened pressure on Moscow.
This does not show direct participation in the war, only limited restraint on ties with Russia.

evidence.title: Human Rights Reports: Custom Report Excerpts - India
evidence.claim: India is a multiparty, federal, parliamentary democracy and the states and union territories have primary responsibility for maintaining law and order, with policy oversight from the central government; Narendra Modi was prime minister for the second time after the 2019 election.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official archived State Department report excerpt with a direct institutional statement about law-and-order authority.
evidence.period_fit: General structure that governed 2022 domestic safety attribution.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Establishes that many security incidents are state-level unless the central government set policy, tolerated them, or used central powers.
contrary_evidence: This is structural context, not proof of any specific Modi action.

reasons.reason: Structural law-and-order context only; it describes federal responsibility, not a direct Modi act.

evidence.title: Human Rights Reports: Custom Report Excerpts - India
evidence.claim: The report says there were reports that the government or its agents committed arbitrary or unlawful killings, police and judicial custody deaths continued, and arbitrary arrest or detention occurred, including torture and mistreatment to obtain confessions.
evidence.locator: Section 1 and subsection d on arbitrary arrest or detention
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official State Department human-rights reporting with direct abuse allegations and custody figures.
evidence.period_fit: Targets India's 2022 conditions as reported in the 2022 country report cycle.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Shows the national security environment under Modi, but many incidents are state or local actions rather than direct central orders.
contrary_evidence: The excerpt does not by itself identify a centralized mass-terror system.
Some abuses were investigated or punished at state level in individual cases.

evidence.title: Human Rights Reports: Custom Report Excerpts - India
evidence.claim: The report says the government restricted internet access, censored online content, monitored users, and blocked telecommunications and internet connections during periods of political unrest; both central and state governments can issue blocking and interception directives.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official archived State Department excerpt with direct operational details about blocking powers and practice.
evidence.period_fit: Directly relevant to 2022 protest and censorship conditions.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Central and state governments share the blocking power, so Modi's attribution is partial and depends on policy use and tolerance.
contrary_evidence: The same legal framework can be framed by the government as security maintenance.
The excerpt does not prove the central office ordered every shutdown.

evidence.title: India: Freedom in the World 2023 Country Report
evidence.claim: Freedom House says the Modi-led BJP government presided over discriminatory policies and increased persecution affecting Muslims, while authorities in June 2022 responded forcefully to protests over remarks about the Prophet and in several regions demolished Muslim-owned property during the year.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Major annual country report with direct 2022 examples and a clear evaluative frame.
evidence.ruler_attribution: National-government and party environment under Modi, though some operational acts were by state authorities.
contrary_evidence: Freedom House still describes India as a multiparty democracy with competitive elections.
The report is evaluative and not a judicial finding.

evidence.title: World Report 2023: India
evidence.claim: Human Rights Watch says the BJP-led government continued systematic discrimination and stigmatization of minorities, especially Muslims, and intensified efforts to silence civil society activists and independent journalists through politically motivated criminal charges, including terrorism.
evidence.locator: Keynote and Civil Society/Freedom of Expression sections
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Major annual rights report with detailed 2022 incidents and direct attribution to the BJP-led government.
evidence.ruler_attribution: This is attributable to Modi's national government and party ecosystem, but not every incident was personally ordered by Modi.
contrary_evidence: The report also notes some institutional channels remained open, including courts and elections.
It is advocacy-oriented and should be balanced with official records.

evidence.title: World Report 2023: India
evidence.claim: Human Rights Watch reports that the National Human Rights Commission registered 147 deaths in police custody, 1,882 deaths in judicial custody, and 119 alleged extrajudicial killings in the first nine months of 2022, while AFSPA remained in force in Jammu and Kashmir and parts of the Northeast, giving security personnel effective immunity from prosecution for serious abuses.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Detailed annual monitoring with specific 2022 figures and institutional assessment.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Shows persistent abuse and impunity under Modi's tenure, but many cases are carried out by state or security forces rather than the PM personally.
contrary_evidence: The same year the central government reduced AFSPA coverage in some northeastern districts.
The figures are reported by an NGO and should be triangulated with official data.

evidence.title: World Report 2023: India
evidence.claim: Human Rights Watch says police in Gujarat publicly flogged Muslim men, authorities in Madhya Pradesh and other states demolished Muslim homes without legal authorization, and police in Jharkhand allegedly used excessive force during June 2022 protests over remarks about the Prophet, killing two people.
evidence.locator: Dalits, Tribal Groups, and Religious Minorities section
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Specific 2022 incidents are identified together with the rights pattern they illustrate.
evidence.ruler_attribution: These were mostly state-level or police actions, but the central government bears partial attribution if it tolerated the pattern or failed to restrain aligned actors.
contrary_evidence: Some demolitions were defended by authorities as legality enforcement.
The police deaths were contested in the original reporting.

evidence.title: India: Persecution of minorities and shrinking space for dissent: Amnesty International submission to the 41st session of the UPR Working Group
evidence.claim: Amnesty says laws and amendments in India threatened freedom of expression and peaceful assembly and discriminated against Muslims and LGBTI people, while raising concerns about human rights defenders, caste discrimination, religious violence, arbitrary deprivation of nationality, indigenous rights, and women's rights.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct 2022 submission to the UN review process with a clear summary of concerns.
evidence.period_fit: Exactly in 2022 and directly relevant to the target year.
evidence.ruler_attribution: This is about the Modi-era legal and political environment; some measures were central, others state-level.
contrary_evidence: It is a submissions document, so the claims are not adjudicated findings.
The submission does not separate every central versus state action.

evidence.title: India JAL 5/2022 - forced evictions and property demolitions against Muslim communities
evidence.claim: UN special rapporteurs said they received information about forced evictions and housing and property demolitions against Muslim minority communities in Madhya Pradesh, Gujarat, and New Delhi that were allegedly ordered by local governments as punishment after intercommunal conflict.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous UN special-procedures communication summarizing alleged abuses and state response.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Primarily local-government conduct, with national attribution only through tolerance, failure to restrain, or policy environment.
contrary_evidence: The communication records allegations and concerns, not a final legal finding.
Local authorities claimed the demolitions were against illegal structures.

reasons.reason: UN special-procedures allegations about local governments; keep the attribution indirect unless central tolerance or direction is separately shown.

evidence.title: Two killed as Muslims and Hindus clash in India
evidence.claim: Reuters reported that two teenagers were killed in Ranchi after clashes that followed derogatory remarks by two ruling-party officials, and that police opened fire to break up the violence while it remained unclear whether the victims were hit by police or rioters.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters wire report with contemporaneous detail and limited attribution uncertainty.
evidence.ruler_attribution: The triggering remarks were from BJP officials, not Modi personally, but the episode reflects his government's broader tolerance problem.
contrary_evidence: Police and rioters were both possible sources of the deaths.
The article does not show a direct Modi order.

evidence.title: Indian state razes Muslim homes after riots over prophet remarks
evidence.claim: Reuters reported that Uttar Pradesh authorities demolished homes of people accused of involvement in riots triggered by remarks made by ruling-party figures about the Prophet Muhammad, while Muslims across India were protesting the anti-Islam remarks.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters wire report republished by the Guardian with direct event details.
evidence.ruler_attribution: The demolitions were carried out by state authorities; Modi's attribution is indirect through national climate and central silence or endorsement.
contrary_evidence: Authorities said the homes were illegal structures.
The source is a wire report, not a legal finding.

reasons.reason: State-level demolition event; it is relevant as national climate evidence, not as direct PM order evidence.

evidence.title: SC puts sedition trials on hold until Govt re-examines it, says affected can seek relief
evidence.claim: The Supreme Court put pending sedition trials and proceedings in abeyance and expected the Centre and states not to register fresh cases or take coercive measures under Section 124A while the government re-examined the law.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous reporting of a major Supreme Court interim order with clear legal effect.
evidence.ruler_attribution: This is a national remedial constraint on coercive law use under Modi's government, not a personal act of violence or protection.
contrary_evidence: The order shows judicial pushback, not that the executive had already reformed practice.
It does not by itself prove lower abuse on the ground.

reasons.reason: Judicial restraint on sedition use; it is a constraint on the executive, not proof of a Modi-directed abuse in itself.

evidence.title: Nirbhaya Fund
evidence.publisher: Press Information Bureau / Ministry of Home Affairs
evidence.claim: The Home Ministry said it had provided Rs 98.86 crores under the Nirbhaya Fund to all states and union territories in 2019-20 and 2020-21 for strengthening existing anti-human-trafficking units and creating new ones, and noted that police and public order are state subjects.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official government release with direct funding and jurisdictional details.
evidence.ruler_attribution: This shows a central-government protective program, but implementation depends on state authorities.
contrary_evidence: It is a financing input, not proof of effective protection outcomes.
The ministry itself emphasizes state responsibility.

evidence.title: English rendering of PMs interaction with those involved in Deogarh Rescue Operation
evidence.publisher: Press Information Bureau / Prime Minister's Office
evidence.claim: Modi praised the rescue teams in the Deoghar ropeway accident, said the operation saved lives, asked for the incident to be documented for future use, and expressed condolences for the families of those who were lost.
evidence.locator: opening paragraphs of the speech text
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct PMO transcript of a 2022 crisis-response event.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct personal crisis-response evidence from Modi, though it is symbolic rather than a policy reform.
contrary_evidence: A rescue speech does not itself establish systemic domestic safety improvement.
It concerns disaster response, not repression.

evidence.title: प्रधानमंत्री श्री नरेंद्र मोदी जी के शांत और समृद्ध उत्तर-पूर्व भारत की परिकल्पना को साकार करते हुए भारत सरकार ने एक बार फिर नागालैंड, असम और मणिपुर में सशस्त्र बल विशेष अधिकार अधिनियम AFSPA के तहत अशांत क्षेत्रों को कम करने का निर्णय किया है
evidence.publisher: Press Information Bureau / Prime Minister's Office
evidence.claim: The release says the disturbed-area notification under AFSPA was fully removed from Tripura and Meghalaya earlier, and from 1 April 2022 was removed from most of Assam and parts of Manipur and Nagaland because the security situation had improved.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official 2022 Hindi PMO release with concrete AFSPA reduction details.
evidence.period_fit: Directly within the target year and in local language.
evidence.ruler_attribution: This is a central-government security-policy change under Modi's leadership, though implementation and ground effects are partly state/security-force dependent.
contrary_evidence: The release is self-congratulatory and does not prove all abuse ended.
AFSPA remained in force in other districts and states.

evidence.title: Cancellation of FCRA Licenses of NGOs
evidence.publisher: Press Information Bureau / Ministry of Home Affairs
evidence.claim: The Home Ministry said it cancelled the FCRA licenses of the Rajiv Gandhi Foundation and Rajiv Gandhi Charitable Trust and reported that 6,677 FCRA registrations had been cancelled between 2017 and 2021.
evidence.locator: opening paragraphs and table of cancellations
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official written-reply release with direct counts and named organizations.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Central-government regulatory enforcement under Modi, though the justification is formal violation rather than a direct safety operation.
contrary_evidence: The government states the cancellations were for legal violations.
Without case-by-case review this could reflect enforcement as well as harassment.

evidence.title: Explained: A stricter policy for accreditation of journalists, and the concerns
evidence.claim: The 2022 accreditation rules introduced cancellation grounds tied to sovereignty, security, foreign relations, public order, decency, morality, defamation, and incitement.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct contemporaneous reporting on an official 2022 policy with specific quoted criteria; strong for the rule text, weaker for intent.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to the Modi government through the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting and PIB.
contrary_evidence: The article notes the policy was presented as an accreditation framework rather than a press ban.
The policy could also be defended as a credentialing rule, not proof of bad-faith enforcement.

evidence.title: Those booked under Section 124A can approach courts for bail: Highlights from Supreme Court order on sedition law
evidence.claim: The Supreme Court said it expected the Centre and states not to register new sedition FIRs, continue probes, or take coercive steps while the law was under review.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: A direct report of a contemporaneous Supreme Court order; high reliability for the order, but it is still secondary reporting.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Indirect attribution to the Modi government because the Centre was the party using and defending the sedition framework, but the immediate actor is the Court.
contrary_evidence: This is a judicial restraint on the executive, not a direct act of censorship by Modi personally.
The government said it was reviewing the law, so the order also reflects institutional correction.

evidence.title: No evidence, Govt didn’t cooperate: SC panel on Pegasus
evidence.claim: The Supreme Court-appointed Pegasus panel found no conclusive evidence on the devices it examined, but the Chief Justice said the central government had not cooperated with the probe.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct reporting of the Supreme Court’s summary of the panel report; reliable for the non-cooperation finding, limited by the panel’s inability to reach conclusive technical proof.
evidence.period_fit: Exact 2022 target-period oversight and surveillance evidence.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to the Modi-led central government as the entity that did not cooperate with the court-appointed probe.
contrary_evidence: The panel did not find conclusive proof of Pegasus use on the devices it examined.
That makes the allegation unresolved rather than proven in this source alone.

evidence.title: India Should Stop Using Abusive Foreign Funding Law
evidence.claim: HRW said the Indian government was harassing the Centre for Promotion of Social Concerns and People’s Watch, including through CBI action under the foreign-funding law, as part of a wider crackdown on civil society.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Detailed human-rights reporting with named organizations, dated events, and explicit attribution to the Indian government.
evidence.period_fit: Directly in-period for early 2022 and squarely within the target year.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct central-government attribution through the CBI/FCRA apparatus under Modi’s administration.
contrary_evidence: The government framed the case as fraud and foreign-funding compliance enforcement.
The report is advocacy-oriented, so its characterization of motive is not itself a legal finding.

evidence.title: India: Media freedom under threat
evidence.claim: RSF and partner groups said Indian authorities were targeting journalists and online critics under counterterrorism and sedition laws, and that India ranked 150th in the 2022 press index.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct rights-organization statement with a clear date, explicit ranking, and specific mechanisms of pressure on journalists.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributed to the BJP-led central government and its enforcement choices; some harassment also came from aligned actors.
contrary_evidence: The statement is a campaign from rights organizations, not a court finding.
The government can argue it was enforcing security and public-order laws.

evidence.title: India
evidence.publisher: Reuters Institute for the Study of Journalism
evidence.claim: The 2022 country report says the Kashmir Press Club was forcibly taken over in January by people allegedly close to local administration, and that new accreditation rules could suspend journalists for work deemed harmful to sovereignty or national security.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Institutional journalism research with explicit 2022 country findings; strong for media-environment context, though the survey portion is not nationally representative.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attribution is partly direct and partly indirect: the central ministry issued the accreditation rules, while the takeover involved local administration and armed police.
contrary_evidence: The report is partly survey-based and limited to English-speaking online users for some metrics.
The Kashmir Press Club episode involves alleged local-administration proximity rather than a court-tested national order.

evidence.title: India's ruling party asks officials to exercise caution on religious issues after Islamic nations protest
evidence.claim: Reuters reported that BJP leaders instructed officials to be extremely cautious about religious remarks after Prophet-related comments triggered protests, and said Muslims were under pressure on worship and hijab issues.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous Reuters reporting on party instructions and the surrounding backlash; strong for the reported directive, weaker for broader causal interpretation.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Party-level attribution is direct to the BJP, and indirectly to Modi as the party’s national leader and government head.
contrary_evidence: The instruction was framed as cautionary messaging rather than overt repression.
It does not by itself prove direct Modi personal authorship of the remarks.

evidence.title: India rushes to quell outrage after insulting remarks on Islam
evidence.claim: Reuters reported that the government sought to calm anger at home and abroad after ruling-party remarks on the Prophet, and that 38 people were arrested for rioting in one northern city.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters-syndicated contemporaneous reporting with a concrete arrest count and direct government response.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Government-level attribution is direct to the Modi administration; the triggering remarks were by BJP officials rather than Modi himself.
contrary_evidence: The government response was calm-down and damage control, not open endorsement of violence.
The arrests were local-law-enforcement actions rather than a national decree.

evidence.title: PM Modi's party set for record win in India’s Gujarat state election
evidence.claim: Reuters reported that Modi’s BJP was headed for a record Gujarat win, with the party on course for its biggest majority in the state and a strong boost before 2024.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct election-result reporting with clear target-year fit; useful for contestability context, but a win alone does not prove electoral fairness.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attribution is indirect but real: this is Modi’s home-state party and his national political base, not a personal electoral decree.
contrary_evidence: A large victory does not by itself prove clean competition.
This source is outcome context, not evidence that Modi respected or violated rules.

reasons.reason: Election outcome context only; it shows contestability, not direct Modi conduct.

evidence.title: Himachal Pradesh results: Difference of 37,974 votes made all the difference for Congress over BJP
evidence.claim: The Congress displaced the BJP in Himachal Pradesh by a margin of 37,974 votes, with both parties contesting the state intensely and the BJP conceding defeat.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous results reporting with vote-share and seat detail; strong for election contestability, though state-level rather than national.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attribution to Modi is indirect but meaningful: his party campaigned heavily and still lost an incumbent state government.
contrary_evidence: This is a state election, not a national transfer of power.
The result is evidence that contestability remained real, not that Modi personally strengthened institutions.

reasons.reason: State-election result context only; it is useful for contestability but not proof of national-level ruler behavior.

evidence.title: PM Narendra Modi and accusations of poll code violation: From 2014 to Congress complaint today
evidence.claim: Congress complained to the Election Commission that Modi’s walk after voting in Ahmedabad amounted to a roadshow, and the EC dismissed the complaint as not established.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct reporting on a live electoral complaint and the EC’s response; reliable for the dispute, but the alleged violation was not upheld.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly about Modi personally, but only as an allegation; the EC rejection means it is evidence of contestation and oversight rather than a proven violation.
contrary_evidence: The Election Commission rejected the claim that a roadshow had been established.
This is therefore better read as a contested complaint than as confirmed manipulation.

reasons.reason: Contested complaint that was not upheld; it should be treated as oversight context rather than a confirmed violation.

evidence.title: Election Commission asks parties to explain how they plan to finance poll promises, draws Opposition fire
evidence.claim: The Election Commission asked parties to disclose how they would finance election promises and why, aiming to standardize information for voters and inform choice.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct reporting on an EC consultation paper and the resulting party criticism; useful institutional context, though not itself a ruler act.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Indirect attribution only: it reflects the electoral environment under Modi’s tenure, not a Modi personal decision.
contrary_evidence: The move drew criticism as overreach from opposition parties.
It is an EC process, not proof that Modi himself was either restrained or manipulative.

reasons.reason: Election Commission process context; it reflects the institutional environment, not a direct Modi act.

evidence.title: Ministry of I&B blocks 16 YouTube news channels for spreading disinformation related to India’s national security, foreign relations and public order
evidence.publisher: Press Information Bureau, Government of India
evidence.claim: The Ministry of Information and Broadcasting used emergency powers under the IT Rules to block 16 YouTube news channels and one Facebook account, saying they spread fake news on security, foreign relations, communal harmony, and public order.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary official release with a precise date, concrete blocking action, and the government’s stated justification.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct central-government attribution under the Modi administration through the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting.
contrary_evidence: The government framed the action as anti-disinformation and public-order protection.
The source itself does not prove the blocked content was genuinely disinformation.

evidence.title: Fiscal Deficit Estimated at 6.4% of GDP in 2022-23
evidence.publisher: Press Information Bureau, Government of India / Ministry of Finance
evidence.claim: The Union Budget 2022-23 set the fiscal deficit at 6.4% of GDP and stepped up capital expenditure by 35.4% to Rs 7.50 lakh crore, with effective capital expenditure at Rs 10.68 lakh crore.
evidence.locator: headline and body paragraphs on fiscal deficit and capital expenditure
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary government budget release with exact figures announced in Parliament.
evidence.period_fit: Exact 2022 budget policy choice for the target year.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to the Modi government through the Union Budget and Finance Ministry.
contrary_evidence: The fiscal deficit remained elevated, so the policy was pro-growth but not fiscally conservative in an absolute sense.
Budget announcements do not prove implementation on their own.

evidence.title: Capital Expenditure Outlay for 2022-23 Increased Sharply by 35.4% with Approximately 67% Spent Between April-December 2022
evidence.publisher: Press Information Bureau, Government of India / Ministry of Finance
evidence.claim: By January 2023 the government said about 67% of the 2022-23 capital expenditure outlay had been spent by end-December 2022, alongside 8,964 National Infrastructure Pipeline projects and record road and waterways output.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary government implementation update with concrete execution figures.
evidence.period_fit: Retrospective evidence on implementation of the 2022 budget within the target period.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to the Modi government’s fiscal and infrastructure execution.
contrary_evidence: The source is a government self-report, so it may accentuate success.
It reports spending volume, not full welfare impact.

evidence.title: IMF Executive Board Concludes 2022 Article IV Consultation with India
evidence.claim: The IMF said the authorities responded to post-pandemic shocks with fiscal measures to support vulnerable groups and front-loaded monetary tightening, with inflation projected at 6.9% in FY2022/23 and risks tilted down.
evidence.locator: press release body and Executive Board Assessment
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous IMF surveillance with explicit findings on policy response and macro conditions.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributed to the Modi government and the RBI policy mix under its institutional framework; monetary policy is partly independent, fiscal measures are directly governmental.
contrary_evidence: The IMF also said public debt sustainability risks had increased.
The source shows stabilization efforts, not a fully successful macro environment.

evidence.title: India: 2022 Article IV Consultation-Press Release; Staff Report; and Statement by the Executive Director for India
evidence.claim: The IMF staff report said India’s world-class public digital infrastructure was facilitating innovation, productivity improvements and access to services, and that further structural reforms were needed for strong and sustainable growth.
evidence.locator: Summary and staff report summary section
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official IMF country report with explicit causal language on digital infrastructure and reforms; still a surveillance document rather than an audit.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Indirect but real attribution to the Modi government because these digital-state capabilities and reform choices were national policy outputs.
contrary_evidence: The report frames these as enabling conditions, not as proof of broad-based welfare gains.
Structural reforms are recommended as still needed, so the record is unfinished.

evidence.title: Indian Economy Continues to Show Resilience Amid Global Uncertainties
evidence.claim: The World Bank said India’s growth for FY2022/23 was estimated at 6.9%, investment was bolstered by the government’s capex push, and inflation averaged around 6.7% for the year.
evidence.locator: press release body and outlook table
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official World Bank India update with explicit growth, investment, and inflation figures.
evidence.period_fit: Retrospective but directly on the 2022-23 period that includes the target year.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Mostly attributable to the Modi government’s fiscal choices, though the outcome also reflects private demand and external conditions.
contrary_evidence: The same source says growth moderated in the second half of FY22/23.
Inflation remained elevated, so the outcome was resilient rather than fully comfortable.

evidence.title: World Bank Approves $47 Million Program to Strengthen India’s Public Sector Capability
evidence.claim: The World Bank approved a $47 million project to support Mission Karmayogi and help build the functional and behavioral competencies of about four million civil servants.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary World Bank project approval with a concrete capacity-building target and clear 2022 date.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to the Modi government because Mission Karmayogi is a national government program.
contrary_evidence: This is capacity-building rather than proof of better policy outcomes.
It speaks to state capability, not to direct competence of every economic appointment.

evidence.title: Annual Report 2022-23
evidence.claim: The RBI said CPI inflation remained above the upper tolerance band for 10 successive months in 2022-23, and that government supply-side measures such as excise duty cuts and lower import duties, together with cumulative repo-rate tightening, helped contain price pressures.
evidence.locator: Economic Review, Inflation in India, and central government finances sections
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary central-bank annual report with explicit diagnosis and policy chronology.
evidence.period_fit: Retrospective on the target year and fiscal year that includes 2022.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Partly direct and partly institutional: government supply-side measures are directly attributable to Modi’s administration, while rate hikes were RBI decisions.
contrary_evidence: Inflation still exceeded the tolerance band for much of the year.
The report stresses that prices were driven by broad global and domestic shocks, not just domestic policy.

evidence.title: RBI releases the Financial Stability Report, December 2022
evidence.claim: The RBI said the Indian economy was facing strong global headwinds but that healthy balance sheets and improving asset quality were supporting financial system resilience, while bank GNPA fell to a seven-year low of 5.0% and NNPA to a ten-year low of 1.3% in September 2022.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary RBI stability assessment with clear quantitative balance-sheet indicators.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Indirectly attributable to the Modi government through the broader macro-policy framework; bank balance-sheet repair is shared with RBI and prior reforms.
contrary_evidence: Financial resilience does not by itself prove broad household prosperity.
The report still flags strong global headwinds.

evidence.title: India central bank raises key rate, says inflation battle not over
evidence.claim: Reuters reported that the RBI raised the repo rate to 6.25% in December 2022, the fifth straight increase, and said inflation remained elevated.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous Reuters report on a major macro policy decision, widely corroborated by RBI records.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Indirect attribution only: the RBI is operationally independent, though the government set the wider macro context.
contrary_evidence: The decision reflects central-bank independence as much as government direction.
Rate hikes are evidence of stabilization pressure, not of economic success.

evidence.title: India | Data
evidence.claim: World Bank data show India’s poverty headcount ratio at $3.00 a day (2021 PPP) was 5.3% in 2022.
evidence.locator: Social section, poverty headcount indicator, most recent value (2022)
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official World Bank country data page with the exact 2022 value visible in the indicator table.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Outcome-only attribution is indirect and mediated by inherited conditions, growth composition, and state implementation.
contrary_evidence: The page does not itself explain the policy drivers behind the poverty rate.
Poverty still remained nontrivial even after improvement.

evidence.title: Page 24 - World Inequality Report 2022
evidence.claim: The India country sheet says the richest 10% held 57% of national income, the poorest 50% held 13%, and the richest 1% held 22%, describing India as poor and very unequal.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Authoritative inequality report with a precise country sheet and widely cited figures.
evidence.period_fit: Pre-2022 baseline and close-in context for the 2022 period.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Indirect attribution only; the figures reflect structural inequality and long-run distribution, not a single-year executive choice.
contrary_evidence: The figures are from 2021, so they are baseline context rather than a 2022 policy outcome.
The report does not isolate Modi-specific causation.

reasons.reason: Baseline inequality context only; it should not be read as a 2022 Modi-era outcome or a direct action.

evidence.title: A total of 61 applicants approved under Production Linked Incentive Scheme For Textiles out of 67 applications received
evidence.publisher: Press Information Bureau, Government of India / Ministry of Textiles
evidence.claim: The government approved 61 applicants under the textiles PLI scheme, with proposed investment of Rs 19,077 crore, projected turnover of Rs 184,917 crore, and proposed direct employment of 240,134.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary implementation announcement with concrete investment and employment targets.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to the Modi government’s industrial policy.
contrary_evidence: Projected employment is not the same as realized jobs.
The scheme is sector-specific and does not prove economy-wide fairness.

evidence.title: Year End Review-2022: Ministry of Rural Development
evidence.publisher: Press Information Bureau, Government of India / Ministry of Rural Development
evidence.claim: The ministry reported that under MGNREGA 11.37 crore households availed employment in 2022, and that 2.11 crore PMAY-G houses had been completed by mid-December 2022.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary year-end implementation report with concrete welfare-delivery figures.
evidence.period_fit: Exact 2022 target-period welfare and rural-income evidence.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to the Modi government’s rural-development delivery apparatus, though execution is shared with states.
contrary_evidence: Household employment under MGNREGA reflects distress as well as support.
The report is a government self-assessment.

evidence.title: Year End Review 2022: Department of Drinking Water and Sanitation, Ministry of Jal Shakti
evidence.publisher: Press Information Bureau, Government of India / Ministry of Jal Shakti
evidence.claim: The government said 10.8 crore rural households had tap-water connections under Jal Jeevan Mission by end-2022, and over 1 lakh villages were declared ODF Plus in 2022.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary government implementation report with concrete infrastructure-delivery figures.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to the Modi government’s national infrastructure and service-delivery program, with implementation shared by states.
contrary_evidence: Tap-water coverage is a delivery metric, not direct proof of welfare gains.
ODF Plus status is an intermediate step, not a final development outcome.

evidence.title: Year End Review-2022: Ministry of Women and Child Development
evidence.publisher: Press Information Bureau, Government of India / Ministry of Women and Child Development
evidence.claim: The ministry reorganized schemes into Mission Saksham Anganwadi and Poshan 2.0, Mission Shakti and Mission Vatsalya, with enlarged outlays and improved nutrition and educational delivery for children and women in 2022.
evidence.locator: opening summary and Mission Saksham Anganwadi and Poshan 2.0 section
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary year-end ministry report with concrete program and budget details.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to the Modi government’s welfare and human-capital policy choices, though outcomes depend on state-level delivery.
contrary_evidence: The source is a ministry self-report.
Program restructuring does not itself prove improved household welfare.

evidence.title: India’s factory growth picks up speed in Oct, hiring at 33-month high
evidence.claim: Reuters reported that India’s factory activity expanded at a stronger pace in October 2022 and firms hired workers at the fastest pace in nearly three years, with the manufacturing PMI at 55.3.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous Reuters survey report with a clear jobs and output signal.
evidence.period_fit: Exact 2022 target-period labour and manufacturing evidence.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Indirect but meaningful attribution to the Modi government’s industrial and macro environment; the survey itself reflects private-sector activity.
contrary_evidence: The PMI is a survey, not a government administrative record.
It shows expansion and hiring, not job quality or income distribution.

evidence.title: Reaching life-saving vaccines to all
evidence.claim: India launched Intensified Mission Indradhanush 4.0 on 7 February 2022 to enhance Universal Immunization Programme coverage across 416 districts in 33 states and union territories after a pandemic-era fall in DPT3 coverage.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Independent WHO feature story with dated 2022 policy and rollout details; strong corroboration for government immunization action.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to the Modi government’s health policy, though implementation depended on states and frontline workers.
contrary_evidence: The source emphasizes coverage catch-up after a pandemic backslide, not a completed outcome.
It documents a launch and rollout plan more than final measured gains.

evidence.title: India crosses a significant milestone in the journey towards Universal Health Coverage - 1,50,000 Ayushman Bharat Health and Wellness Centres operationalized
evidence.publisher: Press Information Bureau, Government of India / Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
evidence.claim: India surpassed 150,000 operational Ayushman Bharat Health and Wellness Centres by 31 December 2022, with more than 86.90 crore screenings, over 8.5 crore teleconsultations, and 1.60 crore wellness sessions conducted through the centres.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary government implementation report with specific, dated delivery metrics.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to the Modi government’s health policy; the rollout was shared with states and health workers.
contrary_evidence: This is a government self-report and may overstate success relative to independent outcome measures.
Counts of screenings and teleconsultations do not by themselves prove equity or quality.

reasons.reason: Government self-report of health-service volume; useful as delivery context, not independent outcome validation.

evidence.title: Year End Review –Ministry of Education
evidence.publisher: Press Information Bureau, Government of India / Ministry of Education
evidence.claim: Samagra Shiksha was aligned with NEP 2020, PM-SHRI was approved to develop 14,500 schools, ICT labs were approved in 1,20,614 schools and smart classrooms in 82,120 schools, and Vidyanjali reached 10.85 lakh students in 2022.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary ministry year-end review with concrete school-system inputs and coverage figures.
evidence.period_fit: Exact 2022 target-period education-policy and implementation evidence.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to the Modi government through central education policy, with delivery shared across states and schools.
contrary_evidence: The source is a ministry self-assessment rather than an external evaluation.
Inputs such as infrastructure and volunteer reach do not directly prove learning outcomes.

reasons.reason: Government self-report of school inputs and reach; useful as implementation context, not proof of learning gains.

evidence.title: Year-End Review-2022: Ministry of Rural Development
evidence.publisher: Press Information Bureau, Government of India / Ministry of Rural Development
evidence.claim: MGNREGA provided employment to 11.37 crore households and PMAY-G had 2.11 crore houses completed by 15 December 2022, with the ministry also reporting broad DAY-NRLM coverage.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary ministry year-end review with clear employment and housing counts.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to the Modi government’s rural-development apparatus, though implementation is shared with states and local institutions.
contrary_evidence: MGNREGA employment also reflects rural distress, not just welfare success.
Completion counts do not by themselves establish quality or durability of housing.

reasons.reason: Government self-report of rural-development counts; useful as service volume, not independent welfare proof.

evidence.title: Year End Review-2022: Ministry of Women and Child Development
evidence.publisher: Press Information Bureau, Government of India / Ministry of Women and Child Development
evidence.claim: The ministry reorganized its welfare work into Saksham Anganwadi & Poshan 2.0, Mission Shakti, and Mission Vatsalya; 40,000 Saksham Anganwadis were identified in FY 2022-23 and more than 15 crore Poshan Maah activities were conducted.
evidence.locator: opening summary and Mission Saksham Anganwadi and Poshan 2.0 section
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary year-end ministry review with concrete scheme redesign and implementation counts.
evidence.period_fit: Exact 2022 target-period child and women welfare policy evidence.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to the Modi government’s social-policy choices, though field delivery depended on states and local workers.
contrary_evidence: The source is a ministry self-report.
Scheme restructuring and event counts do not by themselves prove improved nutrition or protection outcomes.

evidence.title: Year End Review 2022: Ministry of Labour and Employment
evidence.publisher: Press Information Bureau, Government of India / Ministry of Labour & Employment
evidence.claim: eShram had more than 28.5 crore registered workers, ESIC launched an online maternity-claim portal for 58.69 lakh insured women, and the ministry reported 2,297 job fairs in 2022.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary ministry year-end review with large-scale labor-protection and service-delivery figures.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to the Modi government’s labor policy and digital social-protection infrastructure.
contrary_evidence: Registry counts and job fairs do not by themselves prove job quality or income gains.
The source is a ministry self-report rather than independent evaluation.

evidence.title: Year-End Review of Department of Food and Public Distribution– 2022
evidence.publisher: Press Information Bureau, Government of India / Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food & Public Distribution
evidence.claim: PMGKAY continued through Phase VII in 2022 with about 1,118 LMT foodgrains allocated in total, and ONORC exceeded 93 crore portability transactions delivering more than 177 LMT of foodgrains.
evidence.locator: PMGKAY and One Nation One Ration Card sections
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary ministry review with specific program totals and beneficiary-access metrics.
evidence.period_fit: Exact 2022 target-period food-security and portability evidence.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to the Modi government’s food-security policy, with fair-price-shop and state execution shared across levels of government.
contrary_evidence: This is emergency and food-security relief, not proof of long-run food-system resilience.
Administrative distribution totals do not directly show household nutrition quality.

evidence.title: Year End Review 2022: Department of Drinking Water and Sanitation, Ministry of Jal Shakti
evidence.publisher: Press Information Bureau, Government of India / Ministry of Jal Shakti
evidence.claim: By 21 December 2022 more than 10.76 crore rural households had tap-water connections, and 84.83% of schools and 80.79% of anganwadi centres had potable tap water under Jal Jeevan Mission.
evidence.locator: headline and sections on household coverage and public institutions
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary government year-end review with concrete household and institution coverage figures.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to the Modi government’s water-infrastructure program, though delivery was shared with states and local bodies.
contrary_evidence: Coverage figures are administrative and do not fully capture water quality or reliability.
The program was still incomplete in rural India by the end of 2022.

reasons.reason: Administrative tap-water coverage figures; useful for access context, not for independent quality or reliability validation.

evidence.title: Year End Review 2022: Ministry of Tribal Affairs
evidence.publisher: Press Information Bureau, Government of India / Ministry of Tribal Affairs
evidence.claim: The ministry reported that 26.37 lakh tribal students received scholarships through DBT from 1 April to 31 December 2022, and the Cabinet approved Rs 28,920 crore for 452 new Eklavya Model Residential Schools, upgrades to 211 existing schools, and 15 centres of excellence for sports.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary ministry year-end review with clear distribution and institution-building figures for a vulnerable group.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to the Modi government’s tribal policy, with some delivery through state and school systems.
contrary_evidence: Scholarship counts do not prove completion or learning outcomes.
The EMRS approval is a long-term investment, not an immediate welfare result.

evidence.title: Year End Review- 2022 of the Department of Empowerment of Persons with Disabilities
evidence.publisher: Press Information Bureau, Government of India / Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
evidence.claim: The department said it sought to build an inclusive society for persons with disabilities and in 2022 held sign-language events at 3,200 places, signed MoUs with Amazon and Flipkart for skills and employment pathways, and expanded rehabilitation services through new and upgraded centres.
evidence.locator: opening summary and major achievements sections
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary ministry review with concrete inclusion and employment-program details.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to the Modi government’s disability policy, though effects depend on state and private-sector follow-through.
contrary_evidence: Event counts and MoUs do not by themselves prove broad access or equal opportunity.
The ministry framing is self-reported and likely optimistic.

evidence.title: Assets and Liabilities of the Union Council of Ministers (2021-2022) as on 31.03.2022
evidence.claim: Modi's 31 March 2022 asset filing listed Rs 22,382,504 in gross movable assets, no investments in bonds, debentures, shares or units, no immovable property, and a note that the only jointly held property had been donated.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct PMO self-disclosure in a contemporaneous asset filing; strong for what Modi declared, though self-reported disclosures do not independently exclude undeclared interests.
evidence.period_fit: As of 31.03.2022, squarely within the target year.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct self-disclosure attributable to Modi as PM; useful for personal-separation and no-extraction questions, but not a full audit of hidden interests.
contrary_evidence: The filing is self-reported and cannot rule out undeclared assets or benefits.

reasons.reason: Self-reported asset filing, not an audit; it is disclosure context rather than proof of no hidden interests.

evidence.title: IFS Vivek Kumar appointed as PS to PM Modi
evidence.claim: The government appointed Vivek Kumar, an IFS officer of the 2004 batch, as Private Secretary to the Prime Minister at joint-secretary level; the article says he had been in the PMO since 2014.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Secondary reporting, but it quotes a DoPT release and gives a specific named appointment with clear period fit.
evidence.period_fit: Published in May 2022 and directly describes a PMO staffing choice during the target year.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Indirect but relevant: it is a staffing choice in Modi's immediate office and a sign of reliance on a career officer rather than a family or business associate.
contrary_evidence: One professional appointment does not establish the overall staffing pattern of the PMO or government.

evidence.title: No evidence, Govt didn’t cooperate: SC panel on Pegasus
evidence.claim: The Supreme Court-appointed Pegasus committee told the Court that it found no conclusive evidence in the phones examined but that the Central Government had not cooperated with the probe.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: The article reports the Chief Justice's summary of the panel's findings from open court, making it a strong proxy for the judicial record.
evidence.period_fit: The hearing and reported findings occurred in August 2022.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributable to the Central Government under Modi as a matter of state non-cooperation with an independent probe; it does not by itself prove Modi personally ordered concealment or spyware use.
contrary_evidence: The panel also said the evidence it examined was inconclusive on Pegasus use in the sampled phones.

reasons.reason: Institutional noncooperation with the Pegasus probe is relevant, but it is not direct proof of personal dishonesty or spyware use.

evidence.title: Sale of 'less transparent', physical electoral bonds jumps before polls, show RTI replies
evidence.claim: RTI replies showed that the government and RBI had debated electoral-bond design, with the RBI favoring digital-only bonds to reduce misuse while the Finance Ministry emphasized physical bonds to protect donor identity; physical sales rose before the 2022 Gujarat and Himachal Pradesh polls.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Based on RTI-sourced official correspondence and a contemporaneous explanation of the scheme's design choices.
evidence.period_fit: Directly within 2022 and tied to the election cycle that year.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Indirect but material: the design choice belongs to Modi's government and benefited the ruling party's political-finance environment, though it is not personal enrichment evidence.
contrary_evidence: The government argued the scheme still used KYC and banking channels and was meant to preserve donor anonymity from political victimization.

reasons.reason: Political-finance design debate is transparency context, not personal enrichment evidence.

evidence.title: On Electoral Bonds, RTI Body's Order After Election Panel's 'No Info' Reply
evidence.claim: The Central Information Commission directed the Election Commission to swear that it had already supplied all information available with it on electoral bonds and that no further disclosable records existed in its files.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: A PTI-syndicated report of a CIC order; useful as a contemporaneous transparency record but weaker than the underlying order text.
evidence.period_fit: June 2022, directly within the target year.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Indirect to Modi: it concerns the opacity of the electoral-bond regime run under his government, not a personal act of enrichment or concealment.
contrary_evidence: The Election Commission said it had already furnished all available records sought under the RTI request.

evidence.title: Inside Modi's crackdown on the foreign press in India
evidence.publisher: Reuters Institute for the Study of Journalism
evidence.claim: The article reports that between January 2020 and February 2022 foreign correspondents in India described summons by officials, review of files and spreadsheets on negative coverage, visa and permit uncertainty, and growing self-censorship and fear.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Retrospective but well-sourced synthesis from reported surveys, anonymous interviews, and press-freedom reporting; useful for pattern evidence, not a single event record.
evidence.period_fit: The cited surveys cover January 2020 through February 2022, overlapping the target period, though the article itself is later.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Indirect but relevant: it describes the Modi government's environment for scrutiny and foreign correspondents, with attribution limited by anonymized accounts and retrospective synthesis.
contrary_evidence: The piece notes that some restrictions and summonses predated Modi's tenure and that prior governments also expressed displeasure with critical coverage.

reasons.reason: Retrospective synthesis spanning part of 2020-2022; use only as pattern context, not as a clean target-year act-by-act record.

evidence.title: Enabling Logistics Efficiency through Implementation of PM GatiShakti National Master Plan
evidence.publisher: Press Information Bureau, Government of India
evidence.claim: In a special address, the Prime Minister said PM GatiShakti was the first step toward integrated infrastructure planning, efficient coordination, and monitoring, and would reduce time and cost overruns in project execution; he also highlighted the central government's capex rise from Rs 2.5 lakh crore in 2013-14 to Rs 7.5 lakh crore in 2022-23.
evidence.locator: PIB summary of the PM's special address
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct PM speech reported by the government, with a specific policy mechanism and spending figure.
evidence.period_fit: Directly within February 2022 and describing the 2022 program baseline.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to Modi as Prime Minister and to his own stated program.
contrary_evidence: The speech and plan describe intended coordination; they do not by themselves prove later delivery.

evidence.title: Progress related to PM Gati Shakti National Master Plan
evidence.publisher: Press Information Bureau, Government of India
evidence.claim: A written reply said project identification for PM Gati Shakti was ongoing using inputs from infrastructure and economic ministries, data layers were being integrated into the NMP portal, and the EGoS, NPG, and TSU had been constituted and operationalized.

Using your local structured facts and a small external source set, and not using the client matrix.

**Office, Authority, Constraints**
- Modi was India’s Prime Minister in 2022, in his second term that ran from 2019 to 2024 according to the PMO biography. The office is constitutionally the head of government, not an unconstrained executive.
- Under [Article 74](https://www.constitutionofindia.net/articles/article-74-council-of-ministers-to-aid-and-advise-president/) and [Article 75](https://www.constitutionofindia.net/articles/article-75-other-provisions-as-to-ministers/), the PM heads the Council of Ministers, the President acts on ministerial advice, ministers are appointed on the PM’s advice, and the Council is collectively responsible to the Lok Sabha.
- Practical constraints in 2022 were federal and institutional: state and union-territory governments retained primary responsibility for law and order, and rights/media/judicial constraints remained active in the background.

**Retained Sources**
1. [Article 74: Council of Ministers to aid and advise President](https://www.constitutionofindia.net/articles/article-74-council-of-ministers-to-aid-and-advise-president/)  
   - Publisher: Constitution of India  
   - Date: constitutional text; current web page  
   - Precise fact: PM-led cabinet advice is the formal executive channel to the President.  
   - Period fit: permanent constitutional rule; directly relevant to 2022 office power.  
   - Ruler attribution: frames Modi’s authority as institutional, not personal.  
   - Limitations: formal law, not day-to-day practice.  
   - Contrary points: real leverage depends on party discipline, cabinet control, and coalition/parliamentary dynamics.

2. [Article 75: Other provisions as to Ministers](https://www.constitutionofindia.net/articles/article-75-other-provisions-as-to-ministers/)  
   - Publisher: Constitution of India  
   - Date: constitutional text; current web page  
   - Precise fact: the PM is appointed by the President; ministers hold office at the President’s pleasure; the cabinet is collectively responsible to the Lok Sabha.  
   - Period fit: permanent, and the key constraint structure in 2022.  
   - Ruler attribution: supports a state-centered rather than leader-centered reading.  
   - Limitations: says little about informal power inside the BJP/government.  
   - Contrary points: a strong parliamentary majority can still give a PM very high practical control.

3. [Know the PM](https://www.pmindia.gov.in/en/pms-profile/)  
   - Publisher: Prime Minister of India / PMO  
   - Date: current official biography page  
   - Precise fact: the official biography says Modi served as PM from 2014-2019 and 2019-2024, covering 2022.  
   - Period fit: confirms officeholding during the target year.  
   - Ruler attribution: useful for office identity and official self-framing.  
   - Limitations: promotional, not neutral.  
   - Contrary points: should be balanced against independent reporting and rights/economic assessments.

4. [World nuclear forces](https://www.sipri.org/yearbook/2022/10)  
   - Publisher: SIPRI Yearbook 2022  
   - Date: 2022  
   - Precise fact: SIPRI places India among the nine nuclear-armed states and estimates an inventory around 160 warheads at the start of 2022, with ongoing modernization and low transparency.  
   - Period fit: direct 2022 nuclear-capability context for Chapter 1B.  
   - Ruler attribution: state capability under Modi, but not personal responsibility evidence.  
   - Limitations: estimates, not official Indian disclosure.  
   - Contrary points: absence of disclosure means the exact stockpile is uncertain.

5. [Economic Survey 2021-22, inflation section](https://www.indiabudget.gov.in/budget2022-23/economicsurvey/ebook_es2022/files/basic-html/page56.html)  
   - Publisher: Ministry of Finance, Government of India  
   - Date: January 2022 survey publication  
   - Precise fact: the survey says inflation had reappeared globally and that India’s CPI inflation had moderated in late 2021, which is the baseline entering 2022.  
   - Period fit: inherited pre-2022 macro setting.  
   - Ruler attribution: shows the economic conditions Modi inherited at the start of 2022.  
   - Limitations: official framing, before the full 2022 shock sequence.  
   - Contrary points: later 2022 data show the pressure environment worsened.

6. [IMF Executive Board Concludes 2022 Article IV Consultation with India](https://www.imf.org/en/news/articles/2022/12/19/pr22444-india-imf-executive-board-concludes-2022-article-iv-consultation)  
   - Publisher: IMF  
   - Date: December 23, 2022  
   - Precise fact: the IMF says India rebounded strongly from the pandemic downturn, but 2022 policy faced inflation pressure, Ukraine-war fallout, and tighter global financial conditions.  
   - Period fit: excellent end-of-year 2022 macro snapshot.  
   - Ruler attribution: independent macro constraint source, not a praise source.  
   - Limitations: broad macro lens; not ruler-specific.  
   - Contrary points: domestic growth and policy capacity were still relatively strong.

7. [CAPITAL EXPENDITURE OUTLAY FOR 2022-23 INCREASED SHARPLY BY 35.4%](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=1794133)  
   - Publisher: Press Information Bureau / Ministry of Finance  
   - Date: February 1, 2022  
   - Precise fact: the Union Budget 2022-23 raised capex outlay by 35.4% to Rs 7.5 lakh crore and set a 6.4% fiscal deficit target.  
   - Period fit: central 2022 policy response.  
   - Ruler attribution: favorable official evidence of the government’s chosen strategy.  
   - Limitations: a budget announcement is an intent signal, not outcome evidence.  
   - Contrary points: implementation and distributional effects need separate corroboration.

8. [No Modi-Putin summit this year after they met in September- Indian govt source](https://www.euronews.com/2022/12/10/india-russia-modi)  
   - Publisher: Euronews, Reuters wire  
   - Date: December 10, 2022  
   - Precise fact: the piece says Modi and Putin did not hold the annual summit that year and that India had not explicitly condemned Russia’s invasion, while remaining a major buyer of Russian oil.  
   - Period fit: strong 2022 foreign-policy event and constraint marker.  
   - Ruler attribution: directly about Modi’s personal diplomacy.  
   - Limitations: wire reporting from a third-party host; still high value, but not primary government text.  
   - Contrary points: India pursued strategic autonomy rather than alignment.

   - Period fit: directly covers events in Modi’s 2022 period.  
   - Ruler attribution: useful for rights/civil-liberties chapters, with a clear critical lens.  
   - Limitations: annual composite judgment; interpretive by design.  
   - Contrary points: India still had competitive elections and a functioning electoral framework.

   - Precise fact: it describes India as a federal parliamentary democracy, notes states’ primary responsibility for law and order, and lists serious issues including arbitrary killings, torture, internet restrictions, media pressure, and corruption.  
   - Period fit: annual report on 2022 conditions.  
   - Ruler attribution: excellent for Chapters 3B, 4B, and 7B.  
   - Limitations: U.S. government perspective; can overemphasize negatives relative to domestic narratives.  
   - Contrary points: it also recognizes democratic institutions and election competitiveness.

11. [प्रधानमंत्री ने सिविल सेवा दिवस पर लोगों को संबोधित किया](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=1818630)

   - Date: April 21, 2022  
   - Precise fact: Modi’s Hindi remarks stress governance reform, easier public service delivery, and a “nation first” frame.  
   - Period fit: direct 2022 local-language official source.  
   - Ruler attribution: favorable primary source for official intent and governing style.  
   - Limitations: speech, not performance evidence.  
   - Contrary points: useful for stated priorities, not proof of execution.

**Compact Event Map**
- January-February 2022: India entered the year with a post-pandemic rebound, but inflation and fiscal choices were already central policy issues.
- February 1, 2022: the Union Budget emphasized high public capex and fiscal consolidation.
- March-December 2022: democratic competition continued, but rights disputes, communal tensions, and property demolitions remained prominent in external assessments.
- April 21, 2022: Modi publicly framed governance in “common people” and reform terms in Hindi.
- September 16, 2022: Modi publicly told Putin this was “not an era of war,” while India kept strategic autonomy toward Russia.
- End of 2022: IMF assessment still saw recovery, but inflation, war spillovers, and tighter global conditions as the main macro constraints.

- 7B: State Dept, Freedom House, V-Dem, WGI, Transparency International, CAG/Lokpal.
- 8B: Budget/Economic Survey, WGI, IMF, RBI annual reports, NITI Aayog, CAG.
